headline: Critical Rails file-write flaw and Sogou DNS hijack are new; cPGuard supply chain attack now hits thousands of hosting servers

bullets.text: New: The Hacker News reports a critical Rails flaw lets attackers write server files through crafted ImageMagick uploads.
New: The Hacker News reports China-aligned hackers are hijacking Sogou input method DNS requests to deploy a backdoor called DarkVigil.
Growing, cPGuard, now 4 outlets: Help Net Security says a poisoned update hit thousands of web hosting servers. SecurityWeek ties the malicious updates to an OpsShield supply chain attack.

Update, WordPress Core, 3 outlets: BleepingComputer reports CISA flags a WordPress RCE flaw as actively exploited. CISA KEV lists CVE-2026-119977, a race condition added 2026-11-03, with a federal due date of 2026-11-06.
Still active, $6.3B Binance heist, 8 outlets: SecurityWeek reports a rigged coding assignment and an abused AI tool opened the path to the theft.

Still active, Connect Secure, 4 outlets: Ivanti patched two more zero-days chained in attacks, CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527. CISA KEV lists CVE-2026-104935 in the same product, with federal due dates of 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-13.

actions: Find Rails apps that process ImageMagick uploads, follow the Rails project's guidance, and check for unexpected files on those servers.
If you run cPGuard, check servers for the backdoor reported by BleepingComputer and treat data on affected hosts as exposed.
Update WordPress Core for CVE-2026-119977 per vendor guidance; the KEV federal due date is 2026-11-06.
Apply Ivanti's latest Connect Secure patches, covering CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527, and check appliances for compromise.
Find Node-RED instances and Siemens IoT2050 devices, patch CVE-2026-58115 per vendor guidance, and look for backdoors.
Roll out Google's Android patches for CVE-2026-58868 to managed devices as they become available.
